$comment: External agent skills (§7.2). These are NOT awo skills: awo's own skills are flat
markdown in skills/, read by an agent that was told to read them. These are open-
ecosystem skills — a directory with a SKILL.md under .claude/skills/, surfaced by
the harness itself. awo declares them here and `awo skill sync` installs them with
the `skills` CLI, so upstream stays live and the references/ directories that hold
tier `default` installs on a bare `awo skill sync`; tier `catalog` waits to be named
(`awo skill sync seo`). Keep default-tier to things every workspace needs, or the
list turns into noise and stops being read — see rules/use-declared-skills.md.
Nothing here duplicates an awo skill or rule. Deliberately excluded, because we
already have a sharper version and two procedures for one job is worse than one:
skill-creator                  -> skills/author-a-skill (measured on real runs here)

external.name: find-skills
external.summary: use when a task needs a capability this workspace has no skill for — search the ecosystem before hand-rolling the procedure.

external.name: agent-browser
external.summary: use for anything that must be seen in a real browser — visual bugs, UAT journeys, form flows; it is the driver, judging from source is what it replaces.
requires: the SKILL.md is a stub on purpose — run `agent-browser skills get core` for the real workflow

external.name: research
external.summary: use before answering any question you would otherwise answer from memory or one file — it forces primary sources and leaves a cited markdown file behind.

external.name: diagnosing-bugs
external.summary: use the moment something is broken, throwing, failing or slow — build a loop that goes red on the bug first, before proposing any fix.

external.name: seo
external.summary: use when asked to improve search visibility, meta tags, sitemaps or structured data — it audits against Lighthouse rather than guessing at ranking factors.

external.name: vercel-react-best-practices
external.summary: use when writing or reviewing React/Next.js — 70 rules ranked by impact, with waterfalls and bundle size first.

external.name: frontend-design
external.summary: use when building a new UI surface and the look matters — it forces an aesthetic direction up front instead of the default templated result.

external.name: playwright-best-practices
external.summary: use before writing or debugging a Playwright spec — selectors, fixtures and parallelism are where these tests go flaky.
